title: FIIs Turn Selective Buyers: Stake Hikes in 27 Stocks After Two Quarters of Heavy Selling
excerpt: Foreign investors bought a net Rs 13,970 crore in the September quarter after selling over Rs 2.7 lakh crore in the prior two, and filings show four straight quarters of stake hikes in names from BHEL to Groww.
body:
• Foreign institutional investors were net buyers of Rs 13,970 crore of Indian equities in the September quarter (Q2 FY27), after net selling Rs 1,43,150 crore in Q1 FY27, NSDL data compiled by Upstox shows.
  • FIIs raised their stake for a fourth straight quarter in 27 companies, including BHEL, Max Financial, GMR Airports and RR Kabel, according to Ace Equity data.
  • The biggest single-quarter jump in the filings tracked was Groww, where FII holding rose 4.01 percentage points to 10.90%.
  • The buying is selective, not broad: analysts cite US bond yields, the rupee, crude prices and tax structure for the earlier exodus, and stake percentages can also move because of buybacks and new issues.

Foreign investors spent most of 2026 leaving India. In the September quarter, a narrow group of stocks started pulling them back. FIIs were net buyers of Rs 13,970 crore in Q2 FY27, according to National Securities Depository data compiled by Upstox, after net selling Rs 1,43,150 crore in the June quarter and Rs 1,31,122 crore in the March quarter. Within that turn, shareholding filings show a consistent pattern: the same names, quarter after quarter.

Four quarters of quiet accumulation

Twenty-seven companies have now seen FIIs raise their stake for four consecutive quarters, according to Ace Equity data reported by Upstox. Among the largest: Bharat Heavy Electricals, where the FII stake reached 9.94% at the end of September, up from 9.53% in June and 6.23% a year earlier; Max Financial Services, at 48.61%, up from 48.06%; GMR Airports, at 22.95%, up from 21.74%; Bank of Maharashtra, at 6.5%, up from 5.82%; and RR Kabel, at 12.51%, up from 10.67% in June and 8.17% a year earlier. The wider list runs from Indian Bank and ONGC to Biocon, Lupin, LIC and Tata Technologies.

Where the fresh money concentrated

Filings tracked for the September quarter show the sharpest single-quarter increases at Groww, the brokerage platform, up 4.01 percentage points to 10.90%, followed by Shyam Metalics, up 2.32 points, HFCL, up 1.50, and E2E Networks, up 1.26. A separate Upstox ranking of the quarter's strongest FII buying names Nestle India, where foreign holding climbed from 9.74% in Q4 FY26 to 11.7% by September; Eternal, the Zomato and Blinkit parent, from 29% to 33.01%; Tech Mahindra, from 18.59% to 20.76%; and Groww again, from 2.5% in Q4 FY26 to 10.9%. In five of the tracked names, domestic institutions raised their stakes in the same quarter, including Groww and Tata Technologies.

How to read it

Two cautions belong with the numbers. First, this is stock selection inside a weak overall tape: the same period's commentary notes the Nifty's poor run and the headwinds analysts blame for the exodus, from rising US yields and a weaker rupee to crude prices and India's capital-gains tax structure. Second, a rising FII percentage is not always fresh buying; buybacks, qualified institutional placements and new listings can lift the share mechanically. The full filings are compiled at Upstox's FII shareholding tracker. For NRI investors, the usable signal is the persistence: four straight quarters of increases in the same 27 names is a positioning trend, not a one-month trade.
